learning_outcomes.text: Explain the atomic/crystalline structure of materials.
Recognize correlations between chemical bonds and material properties.
Describe microstructural mechanisms and fundamental thermodynamic relationships in materials science.
Name essential mechanical properties of metallic materials and the most important testing methods for their determination.
Explain relationships regarding the behavior of metallic materials at elevated temperatures.
Describe relationships regarding the heat treatment of steels and the resulting microstructures.
Work independently in the field of materials science.
Take responsibility for the services provided.
Work and solve tasks in materials science in teams.
Act fairly and cooperatively and deal with conflicts appropriately.
Actively contribute to the development of materials science topics.

syllabus_topics: Structure and classification of material groups
Independent knowledge acquisition in a specific subject area or strengthening research competence
Familiarization with new topics and critical questioning
assessment_rules: Credit points are awarded upon successful completion of the written exam. Successful participation in the practical course is a prerequisite for taking the exam.
bibliography: Bargel, H.-J./ Schulze, G. (2012): Werkstoffkunde. 11., bearbeitete Auflage, Berlin Heidelberg: Springer-Verlag
